transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I've been making a lot of careless mistakes lately because I'm really struggling to pay close attention to details. It's started to happen so often at work and at home that I felt like I needed to come in and get some help.
I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch that. Could you please repeat or clarify what you'd like me to share next?

Can you tell me if you've also been experiencing any symptoms like restlessness, feeling fidgety, or having trouble staying seated when you need to, or if it's mainly the attention issues that you're struggling with?

I definitely struggle with both attention issues and some restless behaviors. While I don't necessarily have trouble staying seated, I find it really hard to relax or do leisure activities quietly, and I have a very difficult time waiting my turn. On top of that, keeping my focus on tasks and avoiding those careless mistakes is a constant battle for me.
How have these symptoms of inattention and restlessness been affecting your daily life, such as your work, relationships, or overall well-being?

To be honest, I'm not quite sure how to describe the exact impact, as I haven't really thought about it in detail yet. I just know that these issues are happening constantly and it felt like it was finally time to get some help.
Can you tell me more about when you first started noticing these symptoms of inattention and restlessness, and have they been consistent over time or have you noticed any changes in their severity?

These symptoms have been really prominent for about a year and eight months now, though they actually first started back before I turned 12 years old. Since then, they have remained fairly consistent.

Would you say that your restless behaviors and difficulty with quiet leisure activities are as bothersome to you and those around you as your struggles with attention and making careless mistakes, or does one set of symptoms stand out as more problematic?
Both the attention issues and the restlessness are very challenging for me. I'm not really sure which one stands out as more problematic, as they both affect my daily life in different ways.

Can you think of any situations where your restlessness or impulsive behaviors are more noticeable or troublesome to you or others, versus situations where your attention difficulties are more prominent?

I haven't really thought about it or compared the situations that way. Both the attention issues and my restlessness seem to happen quite often, so there isn't really a clear distinction of when one is worse than the other.
How do you think your life would change if you were able to better manage your symptoms of inattention and restlessness, and what would be the most significant improvements you would hope to see?

I haven't thought deeply about the long-term changes, but I would simply hope to be able to focus better on my tasks without making careless mistakes. I'd also really like to feel less restless and impatient in my daily life.

Is there anything else you'd like to share or discuss about your symptoms or experiences that you think might be helpful for me to know as we work towards understanding what's been going on and how to best support you?

Just to summarize, my main struggles really come down to making careless mistakes, finding it hard to do leisure activities quietly, and having a tough time waiting my turn. These difficulties have been going on consistently for about a year and eight months, but I remember having these same issues even as a child before age 12. That is really the bulk of what I've been dealing with.
Is there anything else you feel is important for me to consider or any other questions you have for me before we conclude our discussion today?
No, I don't have any other questions or additional information to share right now. Thank you so much for your time and help today.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of inattention, restlessness, and impulsivity, such as making careless mistakes, difficulty with quiet leisure activities, and trouble waiting their turn, have been consistent over time, starting before age 12. The patient reports both attention issues and restless behaviors as significant problems, with no clear distinction between when one is worse than the other. This presentation aligns closely with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation), which involves a combination of symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity. The previous candidate of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation) seems less likely given the patient's report of significant restless and impulsive behaviors in addition to attention difficulties. Therefore, the current candidate list has been narrowed down to Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation).
